# Equal critical cap mass permits finite rate oscillation at a local deepest anchor

This note strengthens the dormant-defect diagnostic while keeping its
scope explicit. Strictly nested equal-volume caps cannot differ through
positive volume. But finitely many oblique caps can have the SAME exact
critical volume, the SAME actual interior deepest anchor in its fiber,
and different prescribed exponential section rates. Padding gives a
lattice-complete family below the numerical OC threshold with no heavy
fiber, while preserving that local anchor and critical cap menu.
The padded anchor is not globally deepest. Thus the construction does
not satisfy the full selected-minimum hypotheses or refute OC.

## 1. What equal mass actually says for two caps

Let mu be the actual mixed volume and let A,B be measurable sets with
mu(A)=mu(B)=Q. Then

    mu(A\B)=mu(B\A)=mu(A symmetric_difference B)/2.       (1)

If A subset B up to null sets, equality of mass forces their difference
to be null. For two parallel cuts of a full-dimensional fiber whose
intervening strip has positive volume, their masses are strictly ordered.
Consequently a strictly nested continuous family of proper cuts cannot
have one fixed positive critical mass.

This implication does NOT apply after discarding the oblique integer
coefficients: gains on one fiber can equal losses on another.

For any probability law theta of caps ALL of mass Q=beta M, put
W=integral 1_H dtheta. Fubini gives the exact variance identity

    (1/M)integral (W-beta)^2 dmu
      =beta(1-beta)
          -(1/(2M))integral mu(H symmetric_difference H')
                                             dtheta(H)dtheta(H'). (2)

Indeed integral W=Q and
integral W(1-W)=(1/2)integral mu(H symmetric_difference H')dtheta dtheta'.
Thus equal mass controls ordinary overlap exactly; it does not identify
exponentially weighted inverse-volume overlap.

## 2. A symmetric three-fiber core with exact local criticality

Let 0<lambda<=1/4 and let

    A_lambda={(x,y):0<=x<=1, |y|<=x+lambda},
    c=(1,0),
    D_lambda=2c-A_lambda,
    B_lambda=(A_lambda+D_lambda)/2.

At integer bases z=0,1,2 take fibers A_lambda,B_lambda,D_lambda.
They are exactly the integer fibers of the convex hull of the endpoint
fibers at z=0,2. The core mixed set is centrally symmetric about

    Y=(z=1,x=1,y=0).

Y is in the interior of B_lambda. The exact areas are

    |A_lambda|=|D_lambda|=1+2lambda,
    |B_lambda|=3/2+2lambda,
    M_core=7/2+6lambda,
    Q=M_core/2=7/4+3lambda.                              (3)

For the middle-area formula, write A_lambda=A_0+{0}times[-lambda,lambda].
The difference body (A_0-A_0)/2 is a centrally symmetric hexagon of area
3/2 and horizontal width 1. Adding the vertical segment of length
2lambda increases its area by 2lambda; translation by c is irrelevant.

Every closed ambient halfspace containing Y has core volume at least
M_core/2 by central symmetry. Every halfspace through Y with nonzero
continuous normal has boundary of zero mixed volume, so it captures
exactly M_core/2. Hence Y is an actual deepest core point and all such
through-Y caps are actual minimizing caps.

For each 0<t<1 define

    H_t={x+(t-1)z>=t}.                                  (4)

It passes through the SAME point Y. At the three bases its x thresholds
are t,1,2-t. The cap portions in A_lambda and D_lambda are complementary
under central reflection, and the middle cap is half of B_lambda.
Thus every cap (4) has volume EXACTLY Q. Its own-source trace on B_lambda
is proper, with Y interior.

The equal section-centroid condition also holds exactly. The endpoint
section lengths are both 2(t+lambda), the middle section is centrally
symmetric around c, and their weighted average base is 1. The average
continuous x coordinate is 1 and the y coordinate is 0. Thus the full
section centroid is Y, without neglecting integer-coordinate moments.

## 3. Exponential section rates remain freely distinguishable

Use a geometrically normalized positive affine denominator
L_lambda=C_lambda(x+epsilon_lambda) with

    min L_lambda=exp(-T/lambda),                        (5)

where T>0 is fixed. The normalization may use either the core or the
padded family below. All limiting fibers except A_lambda have x bounded
away from zero, so the proof of existence, bounded C_lambda and
reciprocal/log integrability is the same as in the dormant-defect note.

Choose any FINITE list 0<s_1,...,s_k<T and put

    t_(lambda,s)=C_lambda^(-1)exp(-s/lambda)-epsilon_lambda.

For small lambda these thresholds belong to (0,1). The actual caps
H_(t_(lambda,s_i)) all have volume Q, have the same critical anchor Y,
and have section rate exactly s_i on A_lambda. Their continuous normal
is e=(1,0). The threshold on D_lambda is near 2, where L is bounded
away from zero, so it creates no logarithmic section defect there.

The A_lambda inverse-rate defect is

    N_A=2 delta_0 tensor Lebesgue|_(0,T).

For the cap tagged by s, its actual selected inverse defect is

    N_(A,H_s)=2 delta_0 tensor Lebesgue|_(0,s),           (6)

and its inside section defect is 2s delta_(0,s). The actual exterior
logarithmic facet defect is missed by each cap s<T. These are direct
changes of variables, with no substitution of a limiting cap bit.
For prescribed weights p_i summing to one, the finite cap menu therefore
has inverse capture profile

    integral v_(A,H)(R)dtheta(H)
       =2 sum_i p_i 1_(R<s_i) delta_0.                 (7)

Equal critical mass does not collapse these positive rate phases.
All these cap normals are positive-parallel to the zero-face gradient,
so this observation does not create noninside captured mass.

## 4. Exact oscillation identity and loss of ordinary-volume visibility

Take 0<t_1<t_2<1. On A_lambda the first cap contains the second with
volume difference

    D_lambda(t_1,t_2)
       =t_2^2-t_1^2+2lambda(t_2-t_1).                   (8)

On D_lambda the inclusion is reversed with EXACTLY the same volume
difference. Their middle cap is identical. Consequently

    mu_core(H_(t_1) symmetric_difference H_(t_2))
       =2 D_lambda(t_1,t_2),
    mu_core(H_(t_1) intersect H_(t_2))
       =Q-D_lambda(t_1,t_2).                           (9)

In particular, if t_1,t_2 have distinct fixed positive rates s_1,s_2,
the ordinary symmetric difference is exponentially small:

    mu_core(H_(t_1) symmetric_difference H_(t_2))
       =O(lambda exp(-min(s_1,s_2)/lambda)).

Nevertheless their selected inverse defects satisfy the exact limiting
mass difference

    ||N_(A,H_s1)-N_(A,H_s2)||=2|s_1-s_2|>0.             (10)

The cap-volume deficiencies relative to Q are both identically zero.
Thus no bound tending to zero with ordinary cap-volume deficiency or
ordinary symmetric-difference volume can control this inverse-rate
oscillation uniformly along the sequence. The inverse kernel amplifies
an exponentially small exchange between actual fibers to a finite
rate effect. Formula (2) remains true but is correspondingly insensitive
to that effect.

## 5. Padding below the target while retaining local anchors and no heavy fiber

Introduce a second integer coordinate r. Place the core at r=0. At
r=1 put the 25 unit-area fibers

    z=0,1,...,24,
    K_pad=[3,4] times [-1/2,1/2].

Let C_lambda be the convex hull of these two layers. It is a
full-dimensional compact convex body in R^(2+2). Its integer projection
has only r=0,1. At the extreme layer r=0 its sampled fibers are exactly
the core fibers, and at r=1 they are exactly the stated padding fibers.
Thus this is an actual lattice-complete mixed-integer family with

    M=57/2+6lambda,
    Q=7/4+3lambda,
    Q/M<1/9=2^(-2)gamma_2.                              (11)

The strict inequality follows from 9Q=63/4+27lambda<57/2+6lambda
for 0<lambda<=1/4. Every fiber has area at most 2, whereas M/9>3.
In particular no fiber has enough total mass even to equal the target
raw depth M/9; there is no hidden heavy fiber.

Extend (4) by

    H_t={x+(t-1)z-100r>=t}.                             (12)

Every padding point misses (12), since x<=4, z>=0, t<1, r=1.
The core is unchanged. Hence every cap still has EXACT volume Q and
passes through the same own-fiber interior point
Y=(z=1,r=0,x=1,y=0). Every halfspace containing Y captures at least Q
from the symmetric core, and (12) attains Q. Thus Y remains an actual
point of depth exactly Q in the FULL padded mixed set. This statement
controls every oblique ambient halfspace, not merely the displayed menu.
The section-centroid calculation in Section 2 is unchanged because
there is no padding section.

If a finite full-span menu is desired, add the opposite core cuts and
the two y-directed cuts through Y, each also with a -100r term. They
all exclude padding, have volume Q, and their continuous normals include
both signs of both coordinate directions. Thus one may keep an actual
finite balanced menu at this local interior anchor.

## 6. The hypothesis that this construction fails

The point Y is NOT globally deepest after padding. The padding family
is centrally symmetric about

    Y_pad=(z=12,r=1,x=7/2,y=0)

and has total mass 25. Every containing halfspace captures at least
25/2 from padding alone, which is strictly greater than Q. Hence Y_pad
is a deeper mixed-integer point of the full family.

Accordingly the construction does not supply a selected bad minimum,
a common separator covering all deepest sources, or a normal-preserving
physical stress for the full padded body. Those conclusions cannot be
inferred from one valid local critical menu. What is proved is narrower
and useful: equality of actual cap volumes, proper interior own-source
traces, exact full section centroids, a finite balanced menu, lattice
completeness, no heavy fiber, and even the below-target numerical ratio
at that local source do NOT alone suppress inside exponential rate
oscillation. Any new payment must use the coverage of GLOBAL deepest
sources or an equivalent genuinely global selected-minimum condition.
